parties: Zota Health Care Limited (parent); KMHP Ventures Limited (wholly-owned subsidiary)
headline: Zota Health Care acquires 20 lakh equity shares of wholly-owned subsidiary KMHP Ventures via right issue
sum: Zota Health Care Limited has acquired 20,00,000 equity shares of its wholly-owned subsidiary KMHP Ventures Limited through a subscription-based right issue. The transaction was disclosed to the NSE on 22 June 2026.
implication: Intra-group capitalisation via right issue requires careful drafting of subscription terms and board resolutions to ensure compliance with Companies Act gift/benefit provisions and to document arm's length pricing where subsidiary shares are non-listed.
detail: Zota Health Care Limited notified the NSE of the acquisition of 20 lakh (2 million) equity shares of KMHP Ventures Limited, its wholly-owned subsidiary, effected through a right issue subscription mechanism. The transaction structure—a parent company subscribing to a subsidiary's right issue—is typically used to inject capital into subsidiaries while maintaining voting control and avoiding dilution of third-party stakeholders. The exact consideration per share and total deal value were not disclosed in the NSE announcement. Given KMHP Ventures' wholly-owned status pre-transaction, the post-acquisition shareholding remains 100% with the parent.

structure.novel: Right issue mechanism for intra-group capitalisation of wholly-owned subsidiary—capital injection without fresh external fundraising, preserving consolidated control while formalising equity commitment.
